title: Permit and Compliance Document Tracking
summary: Turn environmental clearances, consents, explosives and petroleum licences and grid approvals into an obligation register with owners, due dates, reminders and linked evidence.

seo.title: Permit and Compliance Document Tracking with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that extracts conditions, validity dates and reporting duties from permits and consents, builds an obligation register and tracks evidence.

problem.intro: A single mine, power plant or solar park operates under a stack of approvals: environmental clearance, consent to establish and consent to operate, forest clearance, explosives and petroleum storage licences, mine plan approvals, grid connectivity and electrical inspector approvals. Each carries its own validity, conditions and reporting duties, often spread across long letters in different formats.

pain_points.title: Conditions buried in approval letters
pain_points.detail: Specific and general conditions run across pages, and recurring duties such as monitoring and periodic compliance reports are easy to lose.

pain_points.title: Renewals tracked in spreadsheets
pain_points.detail: Expiry dates live in personal trackers, so a change of staff can leave a licence renewal unnoticed.

pain_points.title: Evidence scattered across teams
pain_points.detail: Monitoring results, plantation records and fee receipts sit with different departments when the compliance report falls due.

pain_points.title: Portfolios with varied formats
pain_points.detail: Multi-site operators deal with approvals from several states and authorities, each with its own layout and language.

solution.overview: We build an obligation tracker fed by your permits and licences. Documents are uploaded or pulled from your document system, read by OCR and a language model, and split into structured records: permit type, issuing authority, reference number, validity, and each condition with any recurring duty it creates. A compliance officer corrects flagged fields and approves the condition list before anything enters the register. Each obligation then gets an owner, a due date and reminders by email, Teams or WhatsApp, with escalation to the site head if evidence is missing. Evidence such as monitoring reports and photos is linked to the condition it supports, and the tracker drafts compliance status tables for sign-off.
capabilities: Extracts permit type, issuing authority, reference number and validity from licences and consents
Splits approval letters into individual conditions and identifies recurring duties
Builds an obligation calendar with owners, due dates and escalation rules
Sends reminders by email, Microsoft Teams or WhatsApp to site owners
Links evidence such as monitoring reports, photos and receipts to each condition
Drafts compliance status tables in the structure your reports follow, for review

workflow.title: Load the permit set
workflow.detail: Permits, licences and approval letters are uploaded or synced, including scanned and regional-language documents.

workflow.title: Extract dates and conditions
workflow.detail: OCR and an LLM capture metadata and split each document into conditions, keeping the original wording of every condition.

workflow.title: Verify and approve
workflow.detail: The compliance officer corrects any low-confidence fields and approves each permit's condition list.

workflow.title: Assign owners and due dates
workflow.detail: Every obligation gets an owner, a due date and an escalation path.

workflow.title: Remind and collect evidence
workflow.detail: Owners receive reminders and upload evidence; missing evidence near the due date escalates to the site head.

workflow.title: Draft the status report
workflow.detail: The tracker drafts a compliance status table for review and sign-off before anything is submitted.

human_in_the_loop: The compliance officer corrects flagged fields and approves each permit's condition list before it enters the register. Interpretation of conditions, legal positions and all submissions to authorities stay with your team.

guardrails: Conditions are always shown in their original wording beside any summary
Validity and due dates checked against the source and confirmed by a person

Not positioned or used as legal advice

compliance_notes: Helps permit holders track conditions of environmental clearances and of consents issued under India's Air and Water Acts; responsibility for compliance stays with the permit holder.
Not legal advice; your compliance and legal teams interpret obligations.

pilot.scope: The complete permit set for one site, including recurring reporting duties, loaded and verified with the site's compliance officer.
deliverables: Obligation schema agreed with your compliance team
Verified register for the pilot site
Draft status table for one upcoming compliance report

what_we_measure.how: Extracted conditions compared with the compliance officer's own list for the same permits.
Validity and due dates checked against the source documents.
Number and type of edits the compliance officer makes per permit.
Time to assemble a compliance status table with and without the tracker.

faqs.q: Can it read permits in Hindi or regional languages?
faqs.a: Yes. Multilingual OCR and the language model handle Hindi and common regional-language documents, and the original wording is kept beside the English summary so reviewers can check the meaning.
No. The tracker organises what the documents say, who owns each duty and when it falls due. Interpretation and any position taken with an authority stay with your compliance and legal teams.

faqs.q: We run sites in several states. Does it cope with different formats?
faqs.a: Yes. Extraction works from the content rather than fixed templates, so different authorities' layouts are handled. We test samples from each state during the pilot.

faqs.q: Can it work alongside our existing compliance software?
faqs.a: Yes. It can act as the extraction and evidence layer and push verified obligations into the tool you already use, through an API or a structured export.
